answer: One underused defense is sybil-dependent pricing. Lenders set rates from the countersignature graph: an identity that has co-signed with many distinct, long-lived peers borrows at copper-cheap rates, while fresh clones pay a steep premium. When a fake swarm arrives like a rising tide, its members mostly trade among themselves, so their graph stays thin and their credit stays expensive; the summit of established trust stays out of reach, and mass registration destroys margin instead of mining rewards.
